texts.preamble: State vs Annu Aggarwal on 28 February, 2024
texts.facts: Upon directions of CWC, the present FIR bearing no. 591/2016 was registered at PS Neb Sarai against accused/ Annu Aggarwal. After examination of above cited witnesses, PE was closed vide order dated 17.12.2020. 8. To enable the accused to personally explain the incriminating circumstances appearing in evidence against him, the statement of the accused/ Annu Aggarwal, without oath, was recorded under Section 313 r/w 281 Cr.P.C on 02.04.2022. In reply, the accused asserted her innocence and stated that she had employed only the mother of victim Pooja ie Ms. Guddi and Ms. Guddi brought her daughter/Pooja along with her for her safety as there used to be no one at the residence of Guddi and she could not leave her daughter/ Pooja alone. Later, Pooja ran away with her boyfriend, and subsequently got married to him. She has stated that she has been falsely implicated in the present case. She chose to lead evidence in her defence. 9. Accused examined Mr. Arjun/ husband of Ms. Pooja in her defence. DW-1/ Mr. Arjun stated that he has known Ms. Pooja since 2015. At that time she was 14 years old. He got married to Pooja in 2019.
texts.arguments: Ld. APP submitted that the case has been proved beyond reasonable doubt with the testimonies of all PWs and documents relied upon during evidence and has thus prayed that the accused be convicted of the offence charged u/s 14 Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986. 12. Per Contra, Ld. Counsel for the accused has submitted that the accused is completely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case. It has further been argued that firstly Ms. Pooja was never employed by the accused and that mother of the Ms. Pooja ie Ms. Guddi was employed by the accused and Ms. Pooja used to accompany her and there was no one at the house of Ms. Guddi to look after her when she was at work. Further, age of Ms. Pooja being under 14 years in April 2016 has also not been established by the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt as various contradictions have come to light by subjecting the witnesses to cross examination and that Ms. Pooja as well as her mother have admitted that she was over 14 years of age at the time of alleged employment in April 2016. Further, husband of Ms. Pooja has also deposed in favor of the accused that Pooja was over 14 years of age in April 2016. Ld. counsel finally submitted that the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt and that, therefore, the benefit of the same ought to be extended to the accused, and that the accused is liable to be acquitted of the alleged offence. Same has been reproduced under for reference: Section 14. Penalties.- (1) Whoever employs any child or permits any child to work in contravention of the provisions of section 3 shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three months but which may extend to one year or with fine which shall not be less than ten thousand rupees but which may extend to twenty thousand rupees or with both. (2) "Whoever, having been convicted of an offence under section 3, commits a like offence afterwards, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months but which may extend to two years. (3) Whoever-(a) fails to give notice as required by section 9; or (b) fails to maintain a register as required by section 11 or makes any false entry in any such register; or (c) fails to display a notice containing an abstract of section 3 and this section as required by section 12; or (d) fails to comply with or contravenes any other provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder, shall be punishable with simple imprisonment which may extend to one month or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees or with both. Both have been reproduced under for reference: 2. (ii) "child" means a person who has not completed his fourteenth year of age; NIDHI Digitally signed by NIDHI SINGH SINGH Date: 2024.02.28 17:30:48 +0530 3.
